dailyInsight.headline: Audit whether your agent manager treats recovery state as its control API
dailyInsight.insight: Kilo Code’s fresh Agent Manager patch supports one bounded audit for teams operating parallel coding agents: identify any file that stores live panel or recovery state, then verify agents change it only through an inventory-backed controller operation rather than direct edits. The public patch adds a list-first move operation for an agent’s worktree and rejects direct writes to the named manager state files.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The new contract requires the caller to obtain live section and session IDs through `action: list`, then pass those IDs to a targeted `action: move`; `sectionID: null` ungroups a worktree. The implementation validates the session and target section, while the write/edit/apply-patch guard refuses direct edits to the persisted manager state. Focused tests establish intended source behavior, not every recovery or concurrent-update outcome.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A stale or invented identifier can reorganize the wrong live worktree, and a convenient state-file patch can collide with a controller that is persisting or restoring the panel. Separating the inventory, mutation API, and recovery file makes a multi-agent controller easier to audit before more automation is allowed to operate it.

actions.audience: Builder or operator of a multi-agent coding workspace
actions.label: Trace one live-state mutation
actions.instruction: In a disposable workspace, choose one agent-manager action that changes live organization or task state. Identify the controller’s read API, its target validation, and the persisted UI/recovery files. Confirm the agent can obtain current identifiers only from the controller and cannot write the persisted state file directly; add one regression test for a stale, unknown, or non-assignable target. Do not use production credentials or modify a live work queue during the drill.

receipts.title: feat(agent-manager): allow sessions to move their worktree between sections or ungroup (#12815)
receipts.supports: Documents the new move operation, the required list-first source of truth for IDs, target validation, nullable ungrouping, and the explicit no-direct-edit rule.

receipts.title: feat(agent-manager): allow sessions to move their worktree between sections or ungroup (#12815)
receipts.supports: Shows the source-level manager protocol, validation, state-path protection, generated SDK contract, documentation, and focused tests used by this audit.

confidence.basis: A fresh merged Kilo Code pull request, its directly inspected commit, the model-facing tool contract, protected-path implementation, and focused tests agree on the list-then-move boundary.

dailyInsight.limitation: These are public source receipts from Kilo Code. They do not establish a released extension version, adoption, safety of every restore or concurrent-update path, or that another agent manager stores and protects state the same way.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise this call if a public regression shows an agent can directly mutate the protected manager state, if a list-derived move targets a different live worktree after a concurrent update without detection, or if the persisted file is documented as the supported control API.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for end-to-end recovery and concurrent-update tests that move a worktree while panel state is saved or restored; that is where the boundary will prove durable or expose a race.
